title: Ordinary higher direct image vanishes on an affine neighbourhood basis
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq S$ an open, $F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $p\in\mathbb N$. Put $Y=f^{-1}U$, $g=f|_U:Y\to U$, and $G=F|_Y$. If $H^p(g^{-1}V,G)=0$ for every affine open $V\subseteq U$, with cohomology computed by the ordinary derived open-section functor [def-sc-open-module-cohomology], then $(R^pf_*F)|_U=0$, where $R^pf_*$ is the ordinary right derived module direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. No quasi-coherence, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or positive-degree assumption is imposed.

source.place: Cohomology, Tags 01E1 (lemma-restrict-injective) and 01E4 (lemma-higher-direct-images); stalk-zero conclusion and affine neighbourhood basis

proof.text: Put Y=f^{-1}U, g=f|_U, and G=F|_Y. Restrict an injective resolution of F to Y. Restriction is exact and preserves injectives, so it is an injective resolution of G. Degreewise sections on g^{-1}V are sections of the original resolution on f^{-1}(U.ι(V)); the section identifications commute with differentials. Applying termwise direct image and exact target open restriction gives an isomorphism between the restricted ordinary higher direct image and the ordinary higher direct image of G along g.

By the cohomology-presheaf theorem, the latter higher direct image is the sheafification of V ↦ H^p(g^{-1}V,G), with the same resolution-derived restriction maps. At every point choose affine neighbourhoods inside any given neighbourhood. The hypothesis makes all values on these affine neighbourhoods zero. Every germ has an affine representative and is the germ of zero; hence every stalk of this presheaf is zero. The cohomology-presheaf comparison is an isomorphism on stalks.

Apply zero detection by module stalks to the higher direct image on U, then transport its zero object property through the restriction comparison of step 1. Degree zero uses the same resolution and comparison. For empty U or empty Y there are no nonzero germs, so these cases are included.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01E1 and 01E4, restricted resolution and affine-basis specialization

theorem isZero_restrict_higherDirectImage_of_affine_basis
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (U : S.Opens) (F : X.Modules) (p : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ (V : U.toScheme.Opens), IsAffineOpen V →
      IsZero ((RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.toRingedSpace p
        ((f ∣_ U) ⁻¹ᵁ V)).obj (Scheme.Modules.restrict F (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι))) :
    IsZero (Scheme.Modules.restrict
      (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived p).obj F) U.ι)
